topSignals.title: German EEG-Novelle/Netzpaket: Redispatch-Vorbehalt now looks headed for removal, with concrete committee dates set (Oct 5/7) and a final vote targeted for Oct 16.
topSignals.text: Following the Sept 24-25 first reading, CDU negotiator Elisabeth Winkelmeier-Becker said the clause "can lead to unintended side effects" and floated alternatives at the grid-connection point instead, while SPD's Nina Scheer indicated her side will "clearly reject" it — the first concrete directional signal since the clause was drafted in May 2026. Expert hearings are now scheduled for Oct 5 (EEG) and Oct 7 (Netzpaket), with final passage targeted around Oct 16, though "open" per the tracker. Material for any German behind-the-meter/islanded SOFC generation model, since removal of the curtailment-compensation clause would improve the economics of grid-parallel operation. klimareporter.de, zfk.de Energiegesetze-Ticker

topSignals.title: Two new ahead-of-print system-level papers land LCOE-usable figures for reversible SOC systems.
topSignals.text: A Journal of Power Sources paper models a 120 kW-class reversible solid oxide cell coupled to thermal energy storage at 60.40% (SOFC-mode) / 88.83% (SOEC-mode) efficiency and a levelized cost of hydrogen of $3.49/kg; a companion Energy Conversion and Management paper finds that pairing rSOC with expanded PV capacity (rather than running it standalone) cuts annualized system cost by over 30% and reaches ~95% energy self-sufficiency. Both flagged for the LCOE model. ScienceDirect (Pan et al.), ScienceDirect (Kourougianni et al.)

Top story — see Top Signal #1:* Germany's EEG-Novelle/Netzpaket now has concrete committee-hearing dates (Oct 5 EEG, Oct 7 Netzpaket) and a targeted final vote around Oct 16, with both coalition negotiators signaling the contested Redispatch-Vorbehalt curtailment clause is likely to be dropped rather than adopted as drafted.

Not previously logged — California data center laws (background, signed Sept 21):* Governor Newsom signed seven bills (AB 1577, AB 2383, AB 2469, AB 2619, SB 886, SB 887, SB 1168) that require data center operators to fund their own grid-upgrade costs (without shifting costs to low-income ratepayers), disclose water use/supply impacts to local governments, and — notably for on-site generation — strip data centers of blanket environmental-exemption eligibility for judicial streamlining unless they demonstrate compliance with state energy, water and fuel-consumption standards. No megawatt thresholds or effective dates specified yet; CPUC to address implementation. Relevant background for any California behind-the-meter SOFC siting case. Governor of California, Utility Dive

lcoe.text: New: Levelized cost of hydrogen of $3.49/kg for a 120 kW-class reversible SOC + thermal-storage system at 60.40%/88.83% round-trip efficiency (Pan et al., J. Power Sources) — cross-check against the model's reversible-mode cost assumptions.

New: >30% annualized-cost reduction and ~95% energy self-sufficiency for an rSOC+PV hybrid microgrid versus a standalone rSOC system (Kourougianni et al., Energy Conversion and Management) — usable for hybrid/microgrid LCOE sensitivity cases.
No new Henry Hub or gas-price datapoint published in the last 24-48h beyond the already-logged Sept 25 EIA "Today in Energy" summer-2026 average ($2.93/MMBtu, 6% below summer 2025).
